caption:
NVIDIA just dropped Cosmos 3: an open omnimodal world model for Physical AI that jointly handles language, image, video, audio, and action in one Mixture of Transformers architecture.

That is the real shift. Older Cosmos stacks kept perception and generation more separate, and modalities mostly stopped at text, image, and video. Cosmos 3 is built so the same backbone can reason over a scene, generate plausible futures, recover actions from change, and post train into robot policy models. NVIDIA and the technical report put Super and Nano sizes on Hugging Face, open code under OpenMDW 1.1, and demos that go from vision language reasoning to pick and place trajectories.

If you only read the marketing, this is a robot learning unlock. If you wear a security hat, it is a blast radius change. When one model plans and can emit actions, the threat is no longer "someone got a weird chat answer." It is "someone poisoned the context, the sensor story, or the post train data, and the effector moved." That is purple team work: attack the closed loop, defend the closed loop.

Defender move this week: treat Cosmos class systems like controllers, not content toys. Require sim before act for any physical effector. Maintain an action allowlist. Put a human approval gate on high impact motions. Log the full input stack that produced a trajectory, not just the final clip.

Would you put an open action model near real robots this year? What gate would have to exist first?

Follow for AI security breakdowns without the fake panic.

narration.text: NVIDIA just shipped Cosmos 3, an open world model that reasons over a scene and can drive robot actions from the same stack.
Language, image, video, audio, and action now share one backbone, so the real risk is not just chat anymore.
When the same model plans and acts, a poisoned prompt or a bad sensor story can end as motion on hardware.
So gate every physical effector. Sim before act, an action allowlist, and a human approval step before anything moves.
The win is not a prettier simulator. It is a world model whose actions you can still contain.
Would you put an open action model near real robots this year? Save this before your next Physical AI risk review.
